newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht stronger, interbank rate eases late.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht stronger, interbank rate eases late.

text.p: The Thai baht firmed against the dollar in late active trade on Monday as Singapore players offloaded dollars following their heavy buying of the U.S. unit last week, dealers said.
"Dollar selling outpaced buying today. Most of the selling came from Singapore," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
The baht rose to 25.894-25.897 to the dollar in late trading from 25.896-25.901 earlier and 25.905-25.915 late on Friday.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the baht/dollar mid-rate at 25.86 against 25.87 on Friday.
Dealers said tightened liquidity also prompted some traders to switch to baht from dollar.
The overnight interbank rate eased to 12.00-13.00 percent late from 14.50-15.00 early in the morning, dealers said.
"Dollar buying was not so strong today. So most local banks were more willing to lend funds," said one money market dealer.
The one-month baht/dollar swap premium eased to 11.50/12.50 satangs per dollar late from 11.75/12.75 earlier.
